name: Antigravity CLI (agy)
notes: Verified against a running install, agy 1.1.19; print, the result record and a resume by conversation id measured again on agy 1.3.0 on 2026-10-06. Keeps no local transcript we could find; instead every print-mode call returns a complete JSON record including the conversation id and full token accounting. The orchestrator persists that record itself, so observation and telemetry are better here than with a passive store — at the cost of only seeing turns it started.
syntax_warning: Go-style flags: the prompt must be ATTACHED to the flag. `agy --print='...'` works; `agy -p '...'` silently takes the next argument as the flag value and drops the prompt. A space-separated form fails without writing anything, which looks exactly like the agent doing nothing.

options.trust_none_why: no flag denies tools - --dangerously-skip-permissions only widens them - so a reviewer runs as an agent of ao's own that only reads, options.reviewer_agent

config.name: {agent}
config.description: ao's reviewer: it reads, and has no tool that writes or runs a command

reviewer_agent.body: You review what the prompt hands you. You read files and write nothing, and you run nothing.

settings.why: an agent's tools leave out the servers the person's own MCP settings attach, and a print run denies a call to one only because no rule allows it

reviewer_agent.note: Measured on agy 1.3.0, 2026-10-06. A print run denies every write and command it cannot ask about, and ends with an empty response and the action in denied_actions. Run as this agent it read the file it was asked to and had no tool to write a file or run a command, and wrote nothing. The person's MCP servers stay attached, Linear's writing tools among them, and a call to one was denied only by that headless rule; excludeDefaultComponents took them away but denied every read too, and --mode=plan changed neither. So ao refuses the reviewer while the person's settings allow more than reading.

answer_record.note: One JSON record on stdout; its response is the answer. A tool the run was denied ends it on an empty response, named in denied_actions, with exit 0 and a notice on stderr (agy 1.3.0). A run that failed says why in the record's error and on stderr, with status ERROR: agy 1.3 ended a review with exit 3 on 'There was a network issue connecting to the server, please try again.', and with exit 1 on 'Eligibility check failed: ... connection refused' where it could not reach its service; those transient are asked again once.

--dangerously-skip-permissions.why: Kept: without it a print run of agy 1.3.0 denies every write and every shell command it cannot ask about (1.1.19 wrote files and soft-denied commands), and the rules that allow a command (permissions.allow) live only in the person's own settings file, which ao does not write; --sandbox isolates commands but runs them unprompted only under a setting too. Read on 2026-09-17 from antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless, antigravity.google/docs/cli/permissions and antigravity.google/docs/cli/sandbox.

busy.note: Print mode is synchronous, so the orchestrator knows exactly when a turn is in flight and does not have to infer it from file mtimes. The two-writer hazard is handled by an in-process lock per conversation id rather than an idle guard.

context.note: No context-percentage signal; approximate from input_tokens against the model's window if the window is known.

directives.todo: Determine whether agy honours an always-included instruction file. Observed: a global rules preamble is replayed into responses, and one two-word prompt consumed 21140 input tokens — check what is being injected before blaming the model.
